raw_response:
I am old now, but I still farm the same 5 mu the way I know works. For my land here in Quzhou, wheat and maize together are the safest. If one side goes badly, the other can still feed us and bring some money. I do not read books, so I look at my own field and what the other people in the village do. Last year wheat did better where I did not skimp on base fertilizer, so this year I will still put enough on wheat. Water from the well costs money, so I will not irrigate too many times, only at the important stages. Maize goes in right after wheat comes off, no delay, because that window is short. I cannot spend too much at once because some people in the family work outside and cash must be kept for daily life, so I use a steady, familiar way, not anything fancy.

For wheat, I will sow in early October with the common local seed people around here use, not expensive seed. I will put basal fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once when the wheat starts to stand up strong in spring. If the weather turns too dry, I will use the well two or three times, mainly before winter, at jointing, and maybe at grain filling if needed. For maize, I will plant as soon as the wheat is harvested in June. I will use hybrid maize seed because maize seed saved at home is not as good. I will put some fertilizer at planting and a second time when the maize is knee high to waist high. If rain is decent, maybe only one irrigation; if summer is dry, then two. I do not spray unless I see a real problem, because medicine costs money.
